title: SIEM export interoperability playbook — customer requirements & connector guidance
summary: Practical interoperability guidance for exporting Redwood audit and telemetry data to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Microsoft Sentinel). Covers RBAC v2 considerations, stable audit-log schema, evidence automation hooks, connector-level transformation patterns, operational SLOs, and a customer onboarding checklist.
body:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook documents recommended patterns and concrete connector behaviors for exporting Redwood Inference security and operational telemetry to customer SIEMs. It is meant for security engineers, solutions engineering, and partner integrations teams supporting Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel deliveries. The goal is consistent, auditable, and resilient exports that preserve RBAC context and support automated evidence collection for customer audits.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Exports are from Redwood control plane (hosted) and optionally from Private (VPC) deployments where enabled.
- Customers may ingest via HTTP intake (HEC / Datadog), EventHub/Log Analytics (Sentinel), or syslog/forwarder patterns.
- Data volumes vary widely: expect small-volume audit events and bursts of higher traffic during incidents or migrations.
- Default retention and sampling policies are configurable per-customer.

High-level architecture patterns (Golden Paths):
1) HTTP native intake (recommended for hosted): Redwood pushes batched payloads to provider HTTP endpoints (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs) with TLS 1.2+/mTLS optional.
2) Push to customer-managed queue (recommended for Private): Redwood writes structured messages to a customer Event Hub / SQS / PubSub; customer pulls into SIEM connector.
3) Forwarder-based (legacy or constrained networks): Redwood emits to an internal forwarder which then maps and posts to SIEM. Use only when direct HTTP is impossible.

Audit log schema (stable core) — recommended canonical fields (each event is JSON):
- timestamp: RFC3339 UTC
- event_id: UUIDv4
- request_id: opaque request trace id
- principal_id: internal user id or service principal id
- principal_type: user | service | api_key | integration
- principal_email: human-friendly identifier when available (redact per PII policy)
- action: CRUD-style action name (e.g., model.deploy, api.generate, rollout.create)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, rollout, key, workspace
- resource_id: stable id or path
- resource_path: human path (org/team/workspace/...)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- outcome_reason: short free-text reason for failures (capped length)
- client_ip: IPv4/IPv6 (if available)
- user_agent: client UA string
- latency_ms: integer (end-to-end request processing)
- bytes_in: integer, bytes_out: integer (when applicable)
- rbac_version: v2
- rbac_snapshot: flattened list of effective roles (see notes below)
- evidence_refs: list of evidence identifiers (see Evidence automation)
- schema_version: 1.0

RBAC v2 considerations (what to export):
- Export the effective role set at time of event (not just assigned roles). For sensitive actions include a minimal role-path (role:name@scope) to enable detection of privilege escalation.
- Never export full policy documents into SIEM by default; instead include references (policy_id) and short hashes. For audit investigations, provide a secure retrieval path to full policy artifacts.
- Map RBAC fields to SIEM role/group constructs: for Splunk, put rbac_version and rbac_snapshot under event metadata; for Datadog use attributes/metadata; for Sentinel map into extended fields on the custom log table.

Evidence automation (how to link artifacts for compliance requests):
- Evidence IDs: each evidentiary artifact (config snapshot, rendered prompt, model weights hash, rollout config) gets a globally unique evidence_id (e.g., evidence::YYYYMMDD::sha256).
- Evidence_refs in audit events are short ids that point to a secure evidence store with retention metadata. DO NOT include raw PII in evidence_refs.
- Automated collection hooks: on key lifecycle events (rollout, rollback, canary-promote, policy-change) snapshot the minimal artifact set and attach evidence_ids to emitted audit events.
- Retrieval: provide a time-limited signed URL to the artifact when responding to a compliance request; log retrieval in audit store.

Connector transformation and mapping patterns (avoid vendor lock and support schema evolution):
- Strategy: keep canonical Redwood schema as source-of-truth. Connectors perform simple ergonomic mappings (copy, rename, type conversions) and attach vendor-specific metadata. Avoid flattening deeply nested data unless required by vendor ingestion.
- Versioning: connector should tag outbound events with schema_version and connector_version. Changes to canonical schema require a minor version bump and changelog entry.
- Field mapping templates (examples):
  - Splunk HEC: top-level event = canonical JSON; map timestamp->_time, host->redwood_host, sourcetype->redwood:audit:1, add index per-customer config. Example payload:
    {
      "time": 1680528000.0,
      "host": "redwood-controlplane",
      "index": "customer-prod",
      "sourcetype": "redwood:audit:1",
      "event": { /* canonical JSON here */ }
    }
  - Datadog Logs: send canonical JSON in "message" or as structured attributes; include "ddsource": "redwood" and dd_trace if available. Use ddtags to annotate customer_id and environment.
  - Sentinel (Log Analytics): map to a custom table (RedwoodAudit_CL) with dynamic columns; push via EventHub or Azure Monitor HTTP Data Collector. Ensure property names end with _s for string columns where needed.

Authentication & authorization for connectors:
- Supported auth modes: HEC tokens (Splunk), API keys (Datadog), OAuth2 client credentials (Sentinel ingest via Logic App / EventHub), mTLS (private deployments), and signed bearer tokens (short-lived JWTs) for push operations.
- Tokens should be rotated regularly and support per-connector scopes. Document recommended TTLs and rotation cadence per customer.

Operational SLOs, observability, and error-handling:
- Delivery latency: median < 2s from Redwood emit to successful POST (where customer endpoint is reachable). Bulkbacks/queueing allowed for high-volume flows.
- Delivery durability: retries with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts; after that, place messages in a dead-letter queue and emit an internal incident event.
- Idempotency: include event_id and request_id so consumers can dedupe.
- Monitoring: connector exposes metrics: events_sent_total, events_failed_total, last_success_timestamp, avg_batch_size, last_http_status. These metrics are instrumented into Redwood Console and can be exposed to customers.
- Alerting: set alert thresholds for >1% sustained error rate, repeated 401/403s, or delivery latency > 10s for 5+ minutes.

Vendor-specific guidance (concise):
- Splunk HEC:
  - Use HEC tokens scoped to index and ingestion role. Prefer HEC over universal forwarder for hosted traffic.
  - Ensure HEC batch_size <= 500 events or <= 5MB per POST to avoid timeouts.
  - Set sourcetype to redwood:audit:1 and maintain index mapping per customer.
  - Example header: Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>
- Datadog Logs:
  - Use Datadog Logs intake API with API key in header. For structured JSON, send batched newline-delimited JSON. Add ddsource: redwood and ddtags:customer:<id>,env:<prod|staging>.
  - Rate limits matter: use a randomized jitter in backoff.
- Microsoft Sentinel (Log Analytics/EventHub):
  - For direct pushes into Log Analytics HTTP Data Collector, respect workspace ingestion schemas and size limits. For larger integrations, prefer EventHub + Azure Function to translate to custom logs.
  - Ensure Azure RBAC roles and managed identity are documented for customer-run ingestion.

Privacy and PII handling:
- Default redact policy: redact principal_email and any free-text prompt content unless explicit customer agreement exists. Use a hashed placeholder for redacted content (sha256).
- Provide a per-customer toggle for redaction vs raw export; require documented agreement for raw prompt export.

Onboarding checklist for new customer SIEM exports:
1) Requirements call: confirm destination type, ingestion method, network egress rules, auth method, index/table names, desired retention, and redaction policy.
2) Security review: exchange key rotation plan, TLS/cert expectations, and expected IP allowlists.
3) Test tenant: configure test endpoint with low-volume stream and validate field mappings and sample events.
4) Performance test: run 10k event burst to measure connector behavior and backpressure handling.
5) Go-live: enable production endpoint during maintenance window and monitor initial 24–72h for errors.
6) Post-go-live review: capture a short report with event counts, delivered bytes, error types, and recommended tuning.

Testing and validation matrix (minimal):
- Schema validation: check presence of required canonical fields and types.
- RBAC fidelity test: create synthetic requests with role changes and validate rbac_snapshot differences appear in SIEM.
- Evidence linkage test: trigger an event that should create evidence artifacts and verify evidence_refs resolve to signed URLs.
- Error handling: simulate 401, 429, and 5xx responses and verify retry/dead-letter behavior.

Appendix: sample small payloads and transforms (literal examples)
- Canonical audit event (compact):
  {
    "timestamp": "2026-02-10T21:14:00Z",
    "event_id": "0a3c9afe-5f4b-4c21-b8f9-1a2b3c4d5e6f",
    "request_id": "req_8b12c",
    "principal_id": "u_12345",
    "principal_type": "user",
    "principal_email": "REDACTED:sha256:abc123...",
    "action": "deployment.create",
    "resource_type": "deployment",
    "resource_id": "d_9876",
    "outcome": "success",
    "latency_ms": 86,
    "rbac_version": "v2",
    "rbac_snapshot": "org_admin@org:team_ops;role:deploy",
    "evidence_refs": ["evidence::20260210::f1e2d3"],
    "schema_version": "1.0"
  }

- Splunk HEC POST example (ND-JSON envelope):
  POST /services/collector/event/1.0 HTTP/1.1
  Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>
  Content-Type: application/json

  {"time": 1707600840.0, "host": "redwood-controlplane", "sourcetype": "redwood:audit:1", "event": { /* canonical event */ }}

Operational notes and gotchas (quick bullets):
- Watch for clock skew: all timestamps should be RFC3339 and validated; connectors should convert to UTC.
- Large prompt fields: truncate at 50k chars by default and emit a truncated flag; customers can opt-in to raw export with a security SLA.
- Connector upgrades: perform matrixed compatibility tests against latest schema and previous two schema versions.
- For Private deployments with strict egress, prefer push-to-customer-queue pattern to minimize outbound dependencies.

Next steps and action items for team:
- Finalize connector compatibility test harness (Jira: SEC-4123).
- Publish canonical schema with JSON Schema and example payloads to Confluence (linked_artifacts entry).
- Run three pilot integrations (one per vendor) and capture tuning notes.

Contact and escalation:
- Playbook owner: Avery Chen (security-and-compliance).
- Primary SE contact: Jordan Patel (solutions-eng).
- Emergency escalation: eng-oncall -> sec-oncall -> product-ops.

This document is intentionally prescriptive in core areas but flexible in vendor-specific transforms. If you need an official connector spec (field-level JSON Schema per vendor), see the linked GitHub PR or open SEC-4123 to request a generated spec for a given customer.
